note: How a scene with a purpose picks the player's path. Moves only, no sentence. The player's character leans toward the reply whose act kinds (`scene-talk.move` in data/content/trait-decisions.json) its traits pull toward most, by the same lean the asker's answers read. Nothing here is a roll; a tie goes to the stable hash of the scene.

tree.about: Owner, Oct 15, night: a scene is a tree, a branch for each thing the player might say. The bounds keep a page readable: past maxNodes only the branch the player's traits lean toward is kept.

maxReplies.checkedAgainst: The owner's four dynamic choices a turn (OWNER-DECISIONS, Oct 14) plus the lie, which he asked for as a fifth reply on the purposes that allow one (Oct 15, night); three read thin, six crowd a page.

maxNodes.checkedAgainst: The review page plays one scene at a time, one path at a time, so every branch must be whole: a pruned branch is a button that leads nowhere. Six hundred nodes holds a five-wide tree five deep with its lie branches.

grounds.about: A request needs its ground on record (owner, Oct 15, night). A donor leans on you only above this share of the money a campaign raised; below it the donor scene is not staged.

donorShare.checkedAgainst: 'Most of' is more than half; a third is the least a donor could claim as 'a lot of what you raised'.

donorFloorMinor.checkedAgainst: A gift big enough that leaning on it reads as pressure, not a joke. Under it the donor is 'one of your donors', with no amount said.

bluntGreeting.about: So scenes do not all open the same way: an asker whose sociability is at or below minus this level skips the greeting and opens on why they came; trait levels run from -2 to 2.
bluntGreeting.checkedAgainst: Batch 20: about one asker in six opens without a greeting, the share of adults a full level or more below the middle on the opening temperament's 10/20/40/20/10 cut.

familyStakes.about: Who at home has a stake in a filing (scenes-from-life, spouse-stake-after-filing). A relative reacts to a filing only when the household's records give them one; the strongest stake casts the relative and gives the scene its facts, and with none the scene is not staged. Read from the household's savings and costs, the filing's election date, and the children's birth dates; nothing is rolled.

runwayShortfall.checkedAgainst: The share of the race the household's savings fail to cover before a relative has money to say about it; at a quarter, savings cover three-quarters of the race. Checked against drawn bench places: household runways run from under two months to most of a year against a race 9 to 10 months away, so the gate admits some households and not others.

youngChildAge.checkedAgainst: The age under which a child at home is not left alone in the evening in most households; local-candidate accounts name young children as the main cost of a run (Toledo Parent, Winston-Salem Chronicle; docs/design/scenes/from-life/spouse-stake-after-filing.md).

timeStrength.checkedAgainst: Where a child at home and a working filer rank against a money shortfall when a relative has both: a half shortfall in savings outranks it, a quarter shortfall does not.

putOffHours.checkedAgainst: Hours of quarrel a night of putting off a relative's stated cost counts for on the tie (the closeness engine reads negative hours as a quarrel, tempered by who holds on to it); one hour is about one talk's length, so a put-off cancels one talk's worth of time together. Checked in the played-world test: the tie ends lower than it began.

gaveStrength.checkedAgainst: Where a candidate's own money in a lost race ranks against a relative who worked it (1): working it is the stronger claim to speak about the loss; money given is half.

familyStakes.answersNote: Which of the relative's answer moves, to a candidate who says they will run again after a loss, mean they are behind the run and which mean they doubt it. Moves only; no sentence.

tieSides.about: Which side of their tie a scene's two people stand, read from the relationship record so a friend and a rival say different things (scene-standard rule 4). A rival is one whose last contact on the tie was a quarrel; a friend is one nearer full closeness than none.

friendCloseness.checkedAgainst: The middle of the closeness scale (0 none, 1 full): a tie at or past it is nearer friendship than no tie. Checked in concession-reported.test.ts: forty hours together put a tie at about 0.46 to 0.5.

endingStrain.about: What an ending that strains a tie writes to closeness (the plan of Oct 28, section 3: each ending's keeps is a write to the engine that owns it). The closeness engine reads negative hours as a quarrel, tempered by who holds on to it. An ending that keeps a favor or a promise is written on the scene's record (facts keeps and ending) for the legislature's obligations and the campaigns engine's promises to read (SG-WORDS-favor-promise-keeps-unread).

relationship-strained.checkedAgainst: One talk's length of quarrel, as familyStakes.putOffHours: a scene left on a strained note cancels about one talk's time together.

trust-lost.checkedAgainst: Twice a strained ending: trust lost (a lie found out, a promise broken to their face) costs more than a talk left unfinished.

timeOfDay.about: When a scene's lines may say what hour it is (words-scene-time-of-day-words). The hour is the player's clock as the scene plays. Before noon the scene is in the morning, and a morning greeting ("Morning. Here to file?") may play; from noon it is the afternoon; both are the daytime, when a line that says the afternoon is still ahead ("I'm vetoing it this afternoon.") may play. From the evening minute on, a line that says the present is the evening ("Thanks for your time tonight.") may play. A scene whose hour no clock keeps sets no mark.

afternoonFromMinute.checkedAgainst: Noon, when ordinary American usage stops saying good morning.

eveningFromMinute.checkedAgainst: 5:00 PM, when the director's offices close (director.json settingHours: an office holds scenes to minute 1020), so a scene in an office is never told as evening. Ordinary American usage starts the evening at about 5 to 6 PM, the end of the usual working day in the American Time Use Survey.

concession.about: Which endings of the concession call (purpose concession-call, scene race-lost) mean the candidate conceded and which mean they would not concede that night. The director marks the reply record conceded yes or no; the press reads the mark and puts the concession, or the refusal, on the public record the paper prints. Ending ids only; no sentence.

letterFacts.about: What a relative's letter may say about the days around it (letter-facts.ts). Read from the person records and the kin-contact engine's records; nothing is rolled.

missedBirthdayDays.checkedAgainst: How long a birthday missed at the reader's table stays on a relative's mind: about four months, which keeps it inside the letters written after it (the engine writes about one letter a month at full closeness) and lets it fade after that.

birthdayNearDays.checkedAgainst: How far ahead a writer says their own birthday is coming up: a month, the cadence of the kin-contact letters, so one letter at most mentions each birthday.

occasionFacts.about: What a celebration or a gathering with someone missing may say about the days around it (celebration-facts.ts, gathering-facts.ts). Read from the life news and the person records; nothing is rolled.

newsDays.checkedAgainst: How far back a relative's own news (a child born, a wedding, a move, new work, an illness) still counts as news at a family occasion: a year, the span in which a family would still be catching up on it.

noticeShortfall.about: How a notice to pay or leave is worded to fit what is owed (owner, Nov 8 playtest: 'that far behind' said of a $14 shortfall). The shortfall is read against the rent the lease asks each month. Under `littleBelow` months of rent the lines call it small (they still say it is owed); from `deepFrom` months of rent they call it deep. In between, the lines say the amount and how long it has run and call it neither. Wording only; the landlord's own weighing of amount and months is the housing engine's.

littleBelow.checkedAgainst: Under half a month's rent is a few days' worth: people call such a gap 'a little short' and not 'behind'. Checked against the played-world test, which prints the owed-to-rent ratio of the notice it reads.

deepFrom.checkedAgainst: Two months of rent owed is where a household says 'months behind' and not 'a little behind' (ordinary usage; a wording line only, no real rate decides anything here). Checked against the played-world test, which prints the ratio of every notice it reads.

departureWhy.about: Why someone is leaving, said only when a record names it (owner, Nov 8: a farewell names the leaving; 'why' only when the records say). Each row is a key in the departure's `reasons` (an event that added to the pull, or a push the moves engine read) or `basis:<destinationBasis>`; the fact it sets is the one the bank's lines require. Rows are tried in order and the first present names the reason; no row present, and no reason is said. Moves only, no sentence.
